exposure: Risk factors for preterm delivery (e.g., threatened preterm labor, short cervix, positive fetal fibronectin)
Signs and symptoms of preterm labor
outcome: Optimal timing of ACS administration (within seven days of delivery)
cohort: Adult pregnant women who received antenatal corticosteroids between January 1, 2011, and December 31, 2019, excluding pregnancies under 23 weeks gestation, incomplete records, or deliveries outside the health system.
finding: A substantial proportion (44.4%) of antenatal corticosteroid administrations were suboptimal (not within seven days of delivery), with threatened preterm labor, short cervix, and positive fetal fibronectin being significantly more prevalent in the suboptimal timing group.
